questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the city was very student friendly, that costs of living weren't too high (rent, utilities, food, going out, etc.), that it would serve as a good learning environment for getting a good grasp on the language and the culture, so as to help me assimilate and better comprehend the country and its people (France, in my case).

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I went to Tours, in the central region, and had a great time. People were very nice and accomodating. I struggled with being shy and lacking confidence in the French that I spoke upon arrival, but most people were kind and understanding, and I improved a whole lot over the 3 and a half months that I spent in the city.
You also not only learn to appreciate the culture and people living there, but also the cultures of all the other exchange students, and even your own. The world is put into perspective, and you learn that we are not so different after all.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy. A few months before departure, the international office at the university provided us with a booklet containing a lot of very useful information regarding accomodation, emergency services, healthcare, student life, general life in France, cultural tips, tips for dealing with homesickness, tips for making friends, etc.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We were all welcomed at the international office upon arrival, where we had to finalise our inscription. Many questions were answered here, and we were provided with the contact info of the international coordinator, who would answer further questions, should they arise. They also organised events for the exchange students the first two weeks of our stay, where a lot of information was presented.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There were very few things that they could not help us with, and those things were usually solved through a Google search or asking a friend.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was fairly doable, I was added to a couple of Facebook groups, and from there it just took some stubbornness. You just had to make sure to write to all the people whose rooms might be of interest and then setting up a meeting to come see the room as soon as possible. That way you give yourself some options. There are many furnished rooms available. In the end, I found a decent room with some good roommates very close to the faculty.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The inner city supermarkets are pretty expensive, so, if possible, try and find the time to go the bigger supermarkets farther from the city centre. Alternatively, there are good online supermarket options with pickup points around the city. Those are usually cheaper than the physical stores.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They made it fairly comprehensible and doable.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was only a matter of making an appointment with the international office, an appointment that took around 30 minutes, and then later speaking with the coordinator assigned to you (usually a teacher), who would help you get an overview of your classes and your schedule.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was an international coordinator, who helped us with general questions, and then our own coordinator, who helped us with university related matters.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was able to take all the classes I wanted, but I think I got lucky. I think I spoke with others who had a bit more trouble with it.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is not much advice to give, the process is fairly intuitive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was decently satisfied with my classes, but it bugged me that the levels seemed to vary quite a lot. There were classes were I felt I was doing high school level work and others were I was completely overwhelmed. I would have a preferred a more narrow spectrum.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: As mentioned above, it varied quite a bit.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was more square and old fashioned, and not as engaging as the teaching done at UCPH, but that is likely due to the more authoritarian school system they still have in France. At UCPH I appreciate that teachers and students see more eye to eye.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Oral French - a class for exchange students to help them improve their spoken French.

Culture and Society - a class for exhange students to help them learn about and understand French culture and society while doing various linguistic exercises.

French oral and written expression - a class on French grammar (so the name of the class is a bit misleading)

English language and history - a class on the history and evolution of the English language.

American civilisation - a class on American history, culture and society

Translation from French to English

Translation from English to French

Introduction to the history of music - a class on classical music from around 1200 to around 1700

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The class on the history of music was quite interesting and the teacher was very charismatic.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Nothing in particular.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Groceries were a bit more expensive than back home.
Bakeries, on the other hand, were so, so cheap, it was lovely to go and get fresh crossaints and bread for around 1 euro a piece.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
For the humble fee of 25€, you could join up to 3 sports classes for the entire semester. I took rock climbing and lindy hop dance classes, both of which were great fun.
Apart from that there is a rich student life with clubs and societies. I didn't take part in that however.
There is also the ESN, which hosted a slew of gatherings for the exchange students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The sport offer is such a good deal, and a great way of meeting people.
The ESN gatherings were a good way to get to know other exchange students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The Loire valley, where Tours is situated, is chock full of castles and beautiful landscapes. The international office often organise trips to these castles on Saturdays. Otherwise, there are great opportunities to go visit the neighboring cities as well as Paris, for that matter.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Not too difficult, the biggest issue was the above mentioned issues with language (confidence in my own level, difficulties in terms of comprehension). The authoritarian school system was a bit tedious as well, but it was managable.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just don't be afraid of speaking to them initially. I made the mistake of letting my lack of confidence get too much in the way initially, but it's the best way to learn. The university offers "tandem sessions" where you can go speak with French students for an hour, half an hour in French, the other half an hour in another language (mostly English).

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Getting adjusted to differentiating between "tu" and "vous" instinctively. Since it's "tu" when speaking to everyone back home, it was a bit weird to have to remember to speak differently to people.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The general openness of the French. It's easy to feel a difference as a Dane, but it was a breath of fresh air that people weren't hesitant at all to strike up conversation with complete strangers. I also appreciated that it is much more common to greet people in general, particularly in shops.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Avoid the CROUS accomodation if you can! It's cheap, sure, but the quality reflects that. I lived there for a week before I found private accomodation. The kitchens are small and really ill equipped; four hot plates and a microwave is all they offer 12-14 people per kitchen. Being almost 2 meters tall, I was also very uncomfortable in the small bed. I was unable to lie down at full length and had to curl up my legs.
2. Don't be afraid to engage with your classmates despite language difficulties. Most of them are happy to help.
3. Be sure to sample some of the excellent restaurants in the city. My recommendations are "Au Chien Jaune" and "Dagobert." For a lovely bar experience check out "Le Serpent Volant."

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If one of your goals is to improve your French, be prepared to encounter a lot of everyday expressions and words you will never have heard of during your formal French studies. It is fun, however, so keep an open mind!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
1. The friends I made from all over Europe. Now I'll have somewhere to crash in almost all of the continent's four corners.
2. The improvements I have made in terms of my French. I have gained much more confidence in my abilities to speak the language and engage with French people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The initial difficulties I faced due to the language barrier. It contributed a bit to a feeling of loneliness and homesickness.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I was luckily not too affected by the pandemic during my stay, but that might not be true for your exchange. Either way, do not hesitate to do an exchange semester, it is such a great experience.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
